text:
No skater in the league has added more wins with his goals than Kyle Connor. By our win-probability numbers his goals have been worth 2.28 wins, first of 499 skaters, and he scored twice in Winnipeg's comeback in Montreal on November 3. He has 13 goals in 17 games, 69 shots, and more than 21 minutes a night.

The Jets around him have been a mess: they went eight straight games without a win, including a 7-0 night in Carolina. Connor's own finishing is running hot (18.8 percent against 14 last season, 13 goals on 8.9 expected), so expect fewer goals per shot. But with him on the ice, his team has scored 6.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve, which has cost him assists. Those two things tend to meet in the middle.

The process is the steady part. He gets to the front of the net (6.7 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 87th percentile, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking), and that does not depend on luck. Our projection still sees a 46-goal season.
headline: Connor is winning games for a team that keeps losing
